page.layout: One page of verse in italic, single column; below the last line a catchword "F" at centre-left and a catchword "Illuc" at right.

p.i: Nec non obsessae prope moenia conditur urbis Sancta fides, pars templa nouant, pars aggere muros Cingere, & aequatas astris attollere turres, Pars fundare domos, opere omnis Boetica feruet.

Et iam finis erat bello, iam Bobdalis ultro Sceptrum fernando, Regiique insignia mittit Ipse habitu vultuque humilis ferrata recludit Limina portarum, & venientes excipit hostes Ibant instructi ordinibus, urbemque petebant Magnanimi Heroes, caroque Isabella marito Ad latus it, pulcra comitum stipata corona, Atque animis sexum, curisque viribus implet.

Pone subit procerum in medio Mendozius Heros Albo inuectus equo, cui sacri insigne senatus Tempora purpureo fulgent umbrata galero Illum candenti tenuissima velat amictu Carbasus, & certo crispatos ordine flexus Centum agit errabunda, sacroque interserit ostro, At circum extremas niuei subtemins oras Finxerat argento, leuisque insperserat auro, Ipsum autem obducto credas transfulgere velo Coccineam chlamydem, atque imis illudere plantis Hos equitum globus, & peditum manus anteit ingens.
Addiderat victo labentem flumine Daurum Mollius, & nitido ludentes aethere centum Pennatas puerorum acies. Proculinde tenebras Horrendas visu, flammamque inamabilis orci

page.notes: The first two lines of the verse are printed with a dropped initial N; the catchwords "F" and "Illuc" are printed at the foot. Some words are blurred by show-through and may be misread, notably "subtemins" and "inamabilis", which are copied as printed.
